PEtab is the exchange format for ODE parameter estimation problems: an SBML model plus tables of
measurements, observables, conditions and parameters, joined by a YAML file. `petab.R` writes the
guide model at the best fit as a PEtab problem and reads it back, as for problems of the
[PEtab benchmark collection](https://github.com/Benchmarking-Initiative/Benchmark-Models-PEtab).

## PEtab export

`exportPEtab()` writes reactions as SBML, observables, errors, data, and the
[parameter transformation](methods-steady-states.html#def-parameter-transformation) `p` with fixed values and values per condition. PEtab 2, the default, has no parameter scales: values
of parameters entering as `exp()` are written on linear scale, with a warning. The [gauge](methods-symmetries.html#def-gauge) of
[Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html) becomes fixed values.

- **State at rest.** `steadyState = pSS` gives a pre-equilibration, a
  [steady state](methods-steady-states.html#def-steady-state) before time 0, shared by both
  conditions. One species per
  [conserved total](methods-steady-states.html#conserved-quantities) starts at the total (`NfkIkb`, `Ikk`), all others
  at 0.
- **Event.** `events = events` writes the [event](methods-sensitivities.html#def-event) at time 0 as the `TNF` value of the condition.
- **Errors.** Imaging readouts get the [error model](methods-objective.html#def-error-model), blots the data standard deviations as noise
  parameters per measurement.

```{r, include = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fits.rds", "fit.R", envir = new.env()))
```

```{r petabexport, warning = FALSE}
```

The export uses the best fit of `fit.R`, loaded from `results/fits.rds`. Each experiment starts
with the pre-equilibration at $t = -\infty$, then the experiment condition at 0:

```{r}
read.delim("results/petab/experiments_oppelt.tsv")
read.delim("results/petab/conditions_oppelt.tsv")
```

## PEtab import

`importPEtab()` builds `prdfn`, the [`obsfn`s](methods-objective.html#def-obsfn) of observables and errors, the `parfn`, data and
`objfn`; a pre-equilibration becomes a `Pimpl()`. With `compile = FALSE`, `compile()` builds the
sources.

```{r petabimport}
```

```{r petabcompile, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# all models of the chapter in one shared object
compile(g, x, pSS, p, e, petab$prd, petab$e, output = "oppelt_petab_guide", cores = 6)
```

```{r petabcompare}
```

The imported problem reproduces the [data term](methods-objective.html#data-term) of `model.R` at the best fit. `petab$bestfit` holds
the nominal values on the problem scales, `petab$parlower` and `petab$parupper` the bounds.

## SBML models

`exportSbml()` writes species with compartments, reactions, parameters and initial assignments;
concentration rates are multiplied by the
[compartment volume](methods-steady-states.html#def-compartment-volume), `importSbml()` divides again.
`importSbml()` returns the equation list in `reactions`, parameter and initial values,
observables, assignment rules and events:

```{r}
sbml <- importSbml("results/petab/oppelt.xml")
names(sbml)
c(states = length(sbml$reactions$states), reactions = length(sbml$reactions$rates))
identical(sort(sbml$reactions$states), sort(reactions$states))
```

`exportSbml(reactions, parameters, inits, filepath)` writes an equation list without PEtab tables.

## Formats and limits

- SBML and PEtab run through reticulate with `python-libsbml`; `DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON` selects the
  interpreter.
- PEtab 1 and 2 are read. `exportPEtab(formatVersion = "1")` keeps scales but writes condition
  expressions that only dMod2 reads.
- `exportPEtab()` writes events at time 0 that replace a state and refuses others.

Reference: `exportPEtab()`, `importPEtab()`, `exportSbml()`, `importSbml()`
